notes: Join to journey data by word_id.
Image dates describe the artwork or object, not the arrival of a word.
Source-declared rights retained for each image; source pages are linked.
Files retain downloaded pixels; card crops are CSS presentation suggestions.
Wikimedia standard thumbnails are used for coffee, sugar, ketchup and typhoon; original image URLs are also included.
Typhoon and ketchup have low-resolution sources; avoid oversized presentation.

images.intro_sentence: A fruit gives a color its name.
images.caption: Orange botanical plate · 1887
images.alt_text: An orange branch with blossoms, a whole orange and a cut fruit on a pale botanical plate.
images.why_this_image: The fruit behind a word that eventually named a color.
images.crop_guidance: Keep the fruit at the bottom of the plate visible; open the full plate from the image credit.
images.editorial_status: selected historical image; date/context must remain in credit

images.intro_sentence: Small grains become a worldwide sweetness.
images.caption: Sugarcane botanical plate · 1890
images.credit_line: Köhler’s Medicinal Plants; Biodiversity Heritage Library
images.alt_text: A historical botanical plate showing tall sugarcane leaves, stalks and flowers.
images.why_this_image: Shows the plant behind sugar’s long commercial and linguistic history.
images.crop_guidance: Use the stalk and sweeping leaves as the focal point; preserve the full original in the detail view.
images.editorial_status: selected historical image; date/context must remain in credit

images.intro_sentence: A spice finds new names and new meanings.
images.caption: Ginger botanical plate · 1883–1914 (publication range)
images.alt_text: Ginger stems and flowers rise from a knotted rhizome in a historical botanical illustration.
images.why_this_image: The recognizable rhizome gives the spice’s changing names a physical anchor.
images.crop_guidance: Frame the rhizome and lower foliage; do not erase the original lettering.
images.editorial_status: selected historical image; date/context must remain in credit

images.intro_sentence: An early arrival makes a long journey.
images.caption: Apricot botanical plate · 1796
images.credit_line: Johann Georg Sturm; illustration by Jacob Sturm
images.alt_text: Apricots, a leafy branch, blossoms and a split fruit with its stone, arranged on an antique plate.
images.why_this_image: An early-ripening fruit whose name took a much longer route.
images.crop_guidance: Keep the cluster of whole fruit prominent; full plate available on click.
images.editorial_status: selected historical image; date/context must remain in credit

images.intro_sentence: A storehouse learns to hold stories.
images.caption: The Gentleman’s Magazine, January issue · January 1731
images.credit_line: Published by Edmund Cave; image via Wikimedia Commons
images.alt_text: A printed title page for The Gentleman’s Magazine, with an engraving of St John’s Gate.
images.why_this_image: Makes the transformation from a storehouse to a collection of writing tangible.
images.crop_guidance: Keep the title and St John’s Gate; this scan labels itself the fifth edition of the January issue, not the first printing.
images.editorial_status: selected historical image; date/context must remain in credit

images.intro_sentence: A king ends up on your restaurant bill.
images.caption: Ivory chess king from Nishapur · 9th–12th century
images.credit_line: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 40.170.150; Rogers Fund, 1940
images.alt_text: A small carved ivory chess king with an abstract arched form.
images.why_this_image: A historical chess king anchors the royal warning behind the word check.
images.crop_guidance: Show the complete object; label it as a chess king because its abstract shape is unfamiliar.
images.editorial_status: selected historical image; date/context must remain in credit

images.image_title: Babur overseeing the Garden of Fidelity
images.caption: Babur overseeing the Garden of Fidelity · 1589
images.credit_line: Baburnama illustration; Victoria and Albert Museum; via Wikimedia Commons
images.alt_text: A two-page Mughal miniature shows Babur and attendants beside an enclosed garden with trees and water.
images.why_this_image: A later garden image echoes the enclosed space in the word’s ancient ancestry.
images.crop_guidance: For a narrow card, focus on the right-hand garden; the complete spread belongs in the expanded image view.
images.editorial_status: selected historical image; date/context must remain in credit

images.intro_sentence: Emptiness becomes something you can count.
images.caption: Bakhshali mathematical manuscript · Date debated
images.credit_line: Bakhshali manuscript; Bodleian Libraries; reproduction via Wikimedia Commons
images.alt_text: A worn birch-bark manuscript fragment covered with mathematical writing.
images.why_this_image: Connects the journey to early Indian mathematical notation; avoid calling this the first zero.
images.crop_guidance: Keep the entire fragment. The image alone does not establish a particular zero symbol or the manuscript’s date.
images.editorial_status: selected historical image; date/context must remain in credit

images.intro_sentence: A mathematician’s name becomes a method.
images.caption: Mathematical handbook, Ms. Ham. 692, folio 36r · 1451
images.alt_text: A parchment manuscript page with handwritten arithmetic, fractions and red headings.
images.why_this_image: The volume includes a Latin translation of al-Khwarizmi’s algebra, illustrating knowledge’s passage into Europe.
images.crop_guidance: This leaf shows arithmetic in a larger handbook; do not call it al-Khwarizmi’s original manuscript.
images.editorial_status: selected historical image; date/context must remain in credit

images.intro_sentence: One drink gives a family of places their names.
images.caption: Coffeehouse in Constantinople · 1846 (source date)
images.alt_text: A warm-toned painting of men gathered at a coffeehouse, with a mosque in the background.
images.why_this_image: A later Ottoman coffeehouse scene evokes the social culture that helped carry coffee’s name.
images.crop_guidance: Keep the gathering in the lower half visible; the source gives 1846, without implying that this is the date the word arrived.
images.editorial_status: selected historical image; date/context must remain in credit

images.intro_sentence: A sauce crosses oceans and changes ingredients.
images.caption: Blue Label tomato ketchup advertisement · 1898
images.credit_line: Curtice Brothers Co.; The American Monthly Review of Reviews; via Wikimedia Commons
images.alt_text: A historical advertisement shows a large Blue Label tomato ketchup bottle beside bold lettering.
images.why_this_image: The bottling and branding of ketchup mark a late chapter of its transformation into a mass-market condiment.
images.crop_guidance: Show the whole bottle and TOMATO KETCHUP wording. Source resolution is only 409 × 599; the pack includes a standard 330px thumbnail. Prefer a compact display and retain the original URL for a higher-resolution replacement.
images.editorial_status: selected historical image; date/context must remain in credit

images.intro_sentence: Several languages meet inside one storm.
images.caption: Typhoon · c. 1915
images.credit_line: Perham Wilhelm Nahl; via Wikimedia Commons
images.alt_text: A monochrome drawing of a tree twisting in strong wind above a turbulent landscape.
images.why_this_image: A historical artwork explicitly titled Typhoon gives the storm a dramatic visual identity.
images.crop_guidance: Show the full artwork. Source resolution is limited to 502 × 654; keep the display width around 250 CSS pixels on high-density screens.
images.editorial_status: selected historical image; date/context must remain in credit
